questions.question: Economics is best defined as the study of how
options: society allocates scarce resources to satisfy unlimited wants
questions.explanation: Scarcity relative to unlimited wants is the central economic problem.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: The real cost of a choice, measured in terms of the next best alternative forgone, is called
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost expresses what had to be given up to obtain something else.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: A production possibility curve illustrates
options: the growth of population over time
the maximum combinations of two goods obtainable from given resources
the relationship between price and quantity demanded
the distribution of income in a country
questions.explanation: Points on the curve are efficient; points inside it waste resources.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: The law of demand states that, other things being equal, as the price of a commodity rises, the quantity demanded
questions.explanation: Price and quantity demanded move in opposite directions, giving a downward-sloping curve.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: A movement along a given demand curve is caused by a change in
options: the price of the commodity itself
questions.explanation: Only a change in the commodity's own price moves you along the curve; other factors shift it.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Which of the following causes a shift in the demand curve for a commodity?
options: A change in the quantity supplied
A fall in the price of the commodity
A rise in the price of the commodity
questions.explanation: Income is a condition of demand, so a change in it shifts the whole curve.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: The price of a commodity falls by 10% and the quantity demanded rises by 20%. Calculate the price elasticity of demand.
questions.explanation: Elasticity = % change in quantity ÷ % change in price = 20/10 = 2.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: When the price elasticity of demand for a good is greater than one, demand is said to be
questions.explanation: Quantity demanded responds more than proportionately to the price change.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Goods that are normally consumed together, such as bread and butter, are called
questions.explanation: A rise in the price of one reduces the demand for the other.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Goods that can be used in place of one another are known as
questions.explanation: A rise in the price of one raises the demand for the other, for example rice and yam.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Equilibrium price in a market is the price at which
questions.explanation: At that price there is neither surplus nor shortage, so the price is stable.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: If the government fixes a maximum price below the equilibrium price, the immediate result will be
questions.explanation: At the lower controlled price, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: The law of diminishing returns operates in the
questions.explanation: It applies when at least one factor of production is fixed.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Total product divided by the number of units of the variable factor employed gives
questions.explanation: Average product is output per unit of the variable factor.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: A fixed cost is a cost which
options: is incurred only at high output
is always equal to total cost
does not vary with the level of output
questions.explanation: Rent on a factory is payable whether or not anything is produced.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: A firm incurs a total cost of ₦5,000 when output is zero. This ₦5,000 represents its
questions.explanation: Costs that remain when output is nil must be fixed costs.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Firms under perfect competition are described as
questions.explanation: Each firm is too small to influence the ruling market price.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: A market situation in which there is only one seller of a commodity is
questions.explanation: A monopolist is the sole supplier and faces no close substitute.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: A market dominated by a few large sellers is called
questions.explanation: In an oligopoly each firm must consider the reactions of its few rivals.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of perfect competition?
options: Barriers to the entry of new firms
questions.explanation: Identical products mean buyers have no reason to prefer one seller to another.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: The most important function of money is to serve as
questions.explanation: Money's primary role is to remove the inconvenience of barter.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: The quality of money that enables it to be used for both small and large transactions is
questions.explanation: Money must be capable of division into smaller units of value.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: The central bank acts as lender of last resort when it
options: lends to commercial banks in temporary difficulty
questions.explanation: It supports the banking system when banks cannot obtain funds elsewhere.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Which of the following is a function of the Central Bank of Nigeria?
options: Accepting deposits from the general public
Buying and selling shares for individuals
questions.explanation: Only the central bank has the sole right of note issue.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: The monetary policy rate is used mainly to control
options: the supply of money and credit
questions.explanation: Raising the rate makes borrowing dearer and reduces credit creation.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Inflation is best described as
options: a fall in the value of exports
a persistent rise in the general price level
a rise in the price of one commodity
questions.explanation: It must be general and sustained, not a once-for-all rise in a single price.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Inflation caused by an excess of aggregate demand over available output is called
questions.explanation: Too much money chases too few goods, pulling prices upward.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: A tax whose rate increases as the income of the taxpayer increases is
questions.explanation: Higher income earners pay a larger proportion of their income.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: A tax levied on goods brought into a country is called
questions.explanation: Import duties are collected at the point of entry by customs.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a direct tax?
questions.explanation: A direct tax is levied on income or wealth and paid by the person who bears it.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Since the 1970s, the largest single source of government revenue in Nigeria has been
questions.explanation: Oil receipts came to dominate federal revenue, replacing agricultural exports.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: A budget in which proposed government expenditure exceeds expected revenue is a
questions.explanation: The gap is normally financed by borrowing.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: The total money value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a year is
questions.explanation: GDP counts output produced inside the country's borders, whoever owns the factors.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Gross national product is obtained by
options: adding net income from abroad to gross domestic product
subtracting depreciation from gross domestic product
adding indirect taxes to national income
questions.explanation: GNP measures output by a country's nationals wherever they are located.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Per capita income is calculated as
options: total population divided by national income
national income divided by total population
questions.explanation: It gives average income per head and is used to compare living standards.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: National income can be measured by the
questions.explanation: All three approaches should in principle give the same total.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: In computing national income, double counting is avoided by
options: counting only final goods or value added
questions.explanation: Counting intermediate goods as well as final goods would inflate the total.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: A country is said to have a comparative advantage in producing a commodity when it can produce that commodity at
options: a lower opportunity cost than other countries
questions.explanation: Comparative advantage rests on relative, not absolute, costs.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Balance of trade is the difference between a country's
questions.explanation: It covers merchandise (visible) trade only.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: The balance of payments of a country records
options: all its economic transactions with the rest of the world
questions.explanation: It includes the current account, the capital account and official settlements.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Specialisation and the division of labour in international trade generally lead to
options: the elimination of all trade barriers
questions.explanation: Each country concentrates on what it produces relatively more cheaply.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: The devaluation of a country's currency is likely to make its
questions.explanation: Foreigners pay less for its goods while its own citizens pay more for foreign goods.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: The Malthusian theory of population holds that
options: population tends to grow faster than the means of subsistence
population growth always raises living standards
population size has no economic effect
food supply grows faster than population
questions.explanation: Malthus argued population grows geometrically while food supply grows arithmetically.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Optimum population is that population which
options: yields the highest output per head
is the largest a country can feed
is equal to the labour force
questions.explanation: Both under-population and over-population give lower output per head.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: A high dependency ratio in a country means that there is
options: a high level of foreign investment
a large proportion of people outside the working age group
questions.explanation: The working population must support many children and elderly people.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Subsistence agriculture is characterised by
options: production mainly for the farmer's own family
specialisation in a single cash crop
questions.explanation: Output is small and little or no surplus reaches the market.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Which of the following is a major problem of agriculture in Nigeria?
options: A shortage of arable land nationwide
questions.explanation: Poor storage causes heavy post-harvest losses, especially of perishables.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Economic development differs from economic growth in that development involves
options: structural and qualitative changes in the economy
only an increase in national output
questions.explanation: Growth is a rise in output; development also changes how the economy is organised.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: Which of the following is the most comprehensive indicator of economic development?
questions.explanation: It combines income with health and education rather than income alone.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.question: The classification of production into primary, secondary and tertiary activities refers to the
questions.explanation: Extraction, manufacturing and services form the three sectors.
questions.subject: Economics
